key_insight: Across Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and small vessel disease, MRI revealed both diagnosis-specific brain changes and shared features associated with cognitive and neuropsychiatric symptoms.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help researchers understand symptom heterogeneity across neurological disorders, but do not establish clinically validated biomarkers.
method: Studied 251 participants spanning three disease groups and age-matched healthy controls.
Combined harmonized cognitive and neuropsychiatric assessments with multimodal MRI using the UK Biobank protocol.
Compared diagnosis-specific imaging features and symptom–brain associations across diagnoses.
evidence_signal: The study replicated established case–control brain differences and linked lower medial frontal pole–motor cortex connectivity to apathy, fatigue, and depression, while cingulum microstructure was associated with cognitive deficits across diagnoses.
watch_item: The reported associations do not establish causality; this study concerns neurodegeneration, not AI-driven cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: Disease-specific versus symptom-specific neuroimaging phenotypes across Alzheimer's Disease, Parkinson's Disease, and Small Vessel Disease
